title: If, Elif, and Else
description: Choose your own adventure! Learn how to make Python execute different code blocks depending on different paths.

content.value: Imagine you are a brave knight in a forest. If you see a green path, you walk left. If you see a red path, you walk right. Otherwise (else), you wait. We do the exact same thing in Python using `if`, `elif` (else if), and `else`!
We use the `if` spell followed by a comparison. If the comparison is True, the indented code underneath gets executed!
What if your score is less than 10? The `else` spell handles everything that doesn't fit the `if` condition.
If you have more than two paths, you can use `elif`. It stands for 'else if' and lets you check another specific condition.
Just like with loops, remember to indent the code under `if`, `elif`, and `else`! Also, don't forget the colon `:` at the end of each path statement!

practice.question: Change the score variable below to 3. What does it print? Then modify the code to add an elif path to print 'Silver!' if the score is greater than or equal to 5.

quiz.question: What does 'elif' stand for in Python?
quiz.explain: `elif` is short for 'else if'. It lets you check another condition when the first `if` turned out False.

quiz.question: What punctuation mark must you put at the end of an 'if' line?
quiz.explain: Every `if` line ends with a colon `:`. It tells Python the indented block below belongs to that `if`.
